newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French 10-year bond futures tumbled in tandem with Bunds on Thursday and bond analysts forecast more weakness on Friday ahead of the first round of the French parliamentary election on Sunday.

"People want to square up their positions ahead of the election," said BIP economist Marie Owens-Thomsen. "I don't think people are shorting the French market ahead of the vote but they would rather sit it out and get back in afterward."
The notionnel settled 74 basis points lower at 128.84, just off the day's lows. Sentiment was also undermined by the weakness of U.S. Treasuries.

Spilling over into the French market was worry about Wednesday's sharp fall in the March U.S. trade gap -- a 19.3 percent decline to $8.51 billion -- which economists said was a strong signal that the U.S. economy was continuing to grow.

"The big change in the markets after yesterday's U.S. trade figure is that people realise that rate hikes are not put on hold forever and that, coupled with some profit-taking ahead of the election, has weakened the market," said another analyst.
Analysts said weighing on the Bund was the decision by the German government to revalue the country's gold reserves to improve its chances of qualifying for monetary union.

"There's no doubt it is hitting the German market," said an economist. "The mark has been going down against other currencies, with the view that there are going to be more rather than fewer members in monetary union."
Germany's decision has been attacked by some economists as an accounting sleight of hand and is seen as undermining Bonn's drive to make the new euro currency as hard as the mark.

One technical analyst said that the notionnel could fall to 128.10. But another said that unless the Bund falls below 100.50, the contract remained relatively sheltered technically as long as it did not close below major support at 128.74.

Economists said French industrial production data released on Thursday was positive but had no market impact. The industrial production index in the manufacturing sector -- stripping out energy and agri-food -- rose 0.4 percent in March following a sharp 3.9 percent recovery the previous month.

"The rebound in manufacturing output leads us to revise upward our estimate for GDP growth in the first quarter, (to) probably over 0.5 percent," economist Philippe Cheval of BNP said in a research note.
Cheval said the intermediate goods industry had shown the strongest performance with stocks falling to low levels while output and orderbooks had risen.
"There is no doubt about the process under way -- a recovery led by inter-industry demands and exports is actually taking place," he said.
June PIBOR lost four basis points to 96.47 while the franc was stable against the mark at 3.3673 per mark.
The negative 10-year OAT-Bund spread narrowed by one basis point to minus 15 from minus 16.
